findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py` to the Scope (and the single-sourced-builder contract test) so the third independent roster copy at line 117–119 is updated to call `build_sibling_roster` alongside `pass1.py` and `fidelity_spot_eval.py`.
evidence: Plan Scope lists only pass1.py and fidelity_spot_eval.py as the two roster copies to unify.
eval_solver.py:117-119: `roster = case.get('sibling_roster') or '\n'.join(f"- {c.get('ticket_id', '?')}: {c.get('title', '')}" for c in children)`
eval_solver.py:120: this title-only roster is passed directly to `passes.pass1_container(..., sibling_roster=roster)`

Plan states: 'Changing only the production copy would make the harness send title-only rosters while production sends AC-bearing ones' — same logic applies to eval_solver.py, which also builds its own roster expression outside the named unification.
findings.finding: A third independent copy of the roster-building expression exists in `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:117-119` — outside `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` — and is not enumerated in the Scope or Testing sections. When `build_sibling_roster` gains per-child AC items, `eval_solver.py` will silently continue producing title-only rosters for container eval fixtures passed to `pass1_container`, creating exactly the divergence the plan says it is designed to prevent.
scenarios: A developer runs a container criterion calibration eval (e.g. G3) via the eval harness. eval_solver.py builds a title-only roster and passes it to pass1_container. The G3 rubric now instructs the reviewer to consult AC items in the roster, but none are present — the eval fires false negatives that the plan specifically designed the AC-item roster to prevent, corrupting calibration data.
findings.suggested_fix: In `eval_solver.py:117`, replace the inline `"\n".join(...)` expression with a call to the shared `build_sibling_roster(children)` helper imported from `pass1.py`, and add `eval_solver.py` to the Scope list and to the `test_roster_builder_single_sourced` contract test.

evidence: Plan says roster 'carries each child's acceptance-criteria items, extracted with `evaluate_plan_clarity(...).ac_items`' but never specifies the serialization format (e.g., whether AC items are indented bullet lines under the child's roster entry, a YAML block, or a flat-appended list).
Current roster format is `'- {ticket_id}: {title}'` per line (pass1.py:154 and fidelity_spot_eval.py:219). The plan says to 'extract' AC items but gives no rendering spec.

`evaluate_plan_clarity(...).ac_items` returns `tuple[str, ...]` of raw checklist strings (e.g. `'- [ ] The criterion ships advisory'`). The G3 LLM reviewer must parse these to discharge the anti-false-positive rule, but the format it will receive them in is nowhere described.

G3 rubric AC test (`test_g3_rubric_cites_roster_ac`) only checks that the rubric 'instructs the reviewer to test against roster's acceptance criteria' — it cannot verify that the format is self-describing for the LLM.
findings.finding: The plan never specifies the rendered format of AC-bearing roster entries that `build_sibling_roster` will emit. The G3 rubric update is described only as instructing the reviewer to test against 'the roster's acceptance criteria', but the actual structure — how `evaluate_plan_clarity(...).ac_items` items (raw checklist strings) are serialized per roster entry — is undefined. This is a processing-rule/schema co-location gap: the G3 rubric needs to know the format to correctly apply the anti-false-positive rule, and `build_sibling_roster`'s output contract is equally unspecified.
findings.location: Approach section ('Where the roster is sent' + 'Make G3's child-coverage audit able to fire'); Scope: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` (`build_sibling_roster` helper); `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G3.md`
scenarios: The G3 reviewer receives a roster with opaquely-formatted AC blocks and cannot reliably match a parent criterion text against sibling AC items, defeating the anti-false-positive purpose.

The `build_sibling_roster` author and the `plan_review_G3.md` author make incompatible assumptions about format (e.g., one uses a YAML-indented block, the other expects a flat list), and no spec resolves the conflict.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach section a concrete rendering spec for roster entries that carry AC items, e.g.: each entry is `'- {ticket_id}: {title}\n  acceptance criteria:\n{indented_ac_items}'` where `indented_ac_items` is each `ac_items` string prefixed with `'    '`. Mirror this exact format in the G3 rubric update so the reviewer instruction is format-aware.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a note to AGENTS.md (or an inline design-doc section in `passes.py` / `pass1.py`) capturing: (a) the invariant that the sibling roster must live in the system-prompt prefix and be included in `parent_tokens`, and (b) the reason `build_sibling_roster` lives in `pass1.py` (passes.py LOC cap constraint), so future maintainers do not silently violate either.
evidence: 'send it once in the byte-stable prefix ... plain string concatenation on the already resolved system prompt'
'passes.py, which at 781 lines is too close to the cap to absorb a new helper'
No AGENTS.md or ADR update appears in the Scope list
findings.finding: The architectural decision to move the sibling roster from per-pairing `instructions` into the byte-stable system-prompt prefix — and its corollaries (roster counted in `parent_tokens`, helper located in `pass1.py` due to `passes.py` LOC cap) — is explained only in the plan's Approach prose. Once this ticket closes, that reasoning lives only in ticket history. No AGENTS.md section, design doc, or ADR captures the invariant (roster must ride the prefix, must be counted in the prefix-token estimate) or the constraint that drove the helper placement (passes.py LOC cap). A future developer maintaining either file has no in-repo signal.
scenarios: A future contributor refactors passes.py, hits the LOC cap, and moves build_sibling_roster there without knowing why it was placed in pass1.py — reintroducing the divergence.
A reviewer modifying the container pass rebuilds the roster in instructions (reverting the prefix placement) without realising the token-estimate and bin-packing depend on it being in the prefix.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short `## Architecture note` block to `AGENTS.md` (or a module-level docstring in `pass1.py`) explaining: 'The sibling roster is concatenated into the container pass system prompt (not per-pairing instructions) so it can be prefix-cached and is counted only once. Its token cost is included in `parent_tokens` to keep bin-packing within the context window. `build_sibling_roster` lives here rather than in passes.py because passes.py is near the 800-LOC cap.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit one-sentence rationale in the plan (or a code comment at the helper definition) stating that `build_sibling_roster` is introduced to prevent active semantic divergence between the two existing call-sites, satisfying YAGNI even with only 2 sites, not speculative Rule-of-Three expansion.
evidence: pass1.py:154: `roster = "\n".join(f"- {c.get('ticket_id')}: {c.get('title', '')}" for c in ctx.children)`
fidelity_spot_eval.py:219: `roster = "\n".join(f"- {c.get('ticket_id')}: {c.get('title', '')}" for c in children)`
Codebase search for 'build_sibling_roster' returns zero hits — does not yet exist
Rule-of-Three: 2 call-sites < 3 threshold
Plan states: 'Changing only the production copy would make the harness send title-only rosters while production sends AC-bearing ones' — active divergence, not hypothetical
findings.finding: `build_sibling_roster` is a proposed abstraction with only 2 confirmed call-sites (pass1.py:154 and fidelity_spot_eval.py:219), which is below the Rule-of-Three threshold for non-premature abstraction. The plan's YAGNI justification (preventing active divergence that would corrupt dogfooding data) is affirmative, but it should be stated explicitly in the plan to guard against future reviewers or tooling treating it as premature.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Single-source the builder' paragraph; pass1.py:154 and fidelity_spot_eval.py:219
scenarios: A future third call-site (e.g. a new eval harness) independently re-implements roster building because the helper's Rule-of-Three justification was not documented and reviewers gate on it.
The plan's own A1 reviewer flags this as premature on a later review pass without the affirmative YAGNI evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: In the 'Single-source the builder' paragraph, append: 'Two call-sites suffice here because the divergence is already live (the two copies will carry different semantics after this change), making the YAGNI bar met for a current done-definition rather than a hypothetical future need.'

findings.finding: fidelity_spot_eval.py builds and passes the sibling roster to pass1_container (lines 219, 251, 260) using identical roster-construction code to pass1.py line 154, yet it is not listed in Scope. If the roster construction in pass1.py changes to carry each child's AC items, fidelity_spot_eval.py's independent roster-building will diverge — it will continue sending title-only rosters to pass1_container, producing inconsistent behaviour between the production path and the spot-eval harness.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract the roster-building logic into a shared helper (e.g. `_build_sibling_roster(children)`) in pass1.py or a shared utility, then call it from both pass1.py and fidelity_spot_eval.py.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the error-handling contract for `build_sibling_roster` when `evaluate_plan_clarity` raises unexpectedly (catch-and-warn with an empty entry, or let it propagate), and add an AC or edge-case test covering that path.
evidence: Plan says: 'A child whose description has no `## Acceptance Criteria` section yields a roster entry without raising' — covers structural absence but not exception from the underlying helper
Plan says: 'extracted with `evaluate_plan_clarity(...).ac_items` (`src/rebar/_plan_clarity.py:96`) — the same helper the DET floor uses' — no error contract stated for unexpected failures
No AC or test specifies behavior when `evaluate_plan_clarity` raises (e.g., malformed UTF-8, unexpected schema)
findings.finding: The plan introduces `build_sibling_roster` as a new failure point that calls `evaluate_plan_clarity(...)` on each child description, but specifies graceful degradation only for the 'no AC section' and 'no children' structural cases. If `evaluate_plan_clarity` raises an unexpected exception (e.g., on a malformed or unusually structured child description), the plan is silent on whether that exception propagates and aborts the entire container-pass review or is caught and converted to a safe empty-roster entry. The AC does not include a test for this failure mode.
findings.location: Approach section — 'build_sibling_roster' description; Testing section — 'Edge' test cases; AC line: 'A child description with no `## Acceptance Criteria` section, and a parent with no children, each produce a roster without raising'
scenarios: A child plan with a pathological description (e.g., binary content, extremely nested structure) causes `evaluate_plan_clarity` to raise; the exception propagates and silently aborts G3 review for the entire parent, with no log or fallback
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `try/except Exception` guard inside `build_sibling_roster` per child, log a warning with the child id, and return an entry with empty `ac_items`. Add an AC: 'A child description that causes `evaluate_plan_clarity` to raise yields a roster entry with empty ac_items and logs a warning, without aborting roster construction.'
